caption:
Nine hours of sitting has left Mr Turtle's lower back aching, and his first remedial massage is coming up. Here's what to expect.

It starts with questions: where it hurts, what eases or aggravates it, and your health history. Lower back pain often involves the muscles around it, so expect work through the back, glutes and hips. Firm doesn't have to mean painful, and you can ask for lighter or firmer pressure at any time.

Massage complements walking and strength work rather than replacing them. Pain spreading down a leg, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel changes, or pain after a fall should be assessed by a GP or physio first.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio tailor each session. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
